source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #262 (branch fix/187-memory-access-flatten at merge commit 4c12a5f3dcdd85e91b52db1363655caf35c5dad2 — branch head 31e80be68aa9358cdb86994831662eca7c0a7f70 with current main 3121c3a6efe48cd625b9b9d4e16469cbda7de099 merged in without conflicts, so the pull-request run built the same tree; ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45096189255 and 45096200688 against the branch and pull-request run 45096136125, which built the same tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #262 (#187, flatten scalar linear-memory access to one compare against a frame-cached (base, len)). The PR snapshots the default local memory's (base, committed len) in ExecuteContext alongside the memory pointer, adds DefaultLocalMemoryView in crates/telomere/src/common.rs (a single u64 compare, offset + N <= len, returning MemoryIndexOutOfRange), routes every scalar handler on the default local path through it (94 call sites plus the hand-written helpers in crates/telomere/src/runtime/vm/memory.rs, store_internal_local in vm.rs, the u32 store in superinstructions.rs, and the u16 load in call.rs), and re-snapshots the length in the two memory.grow handlers; shared memory keeps the previous locked path because its cached pointer is null. The PR's only other change is a new integration test file, which is not linked into the embedder. Attribution was isolated by measuring current main (3121c3a) alone (workflow_dispatch run 45096211898, gate success): it reproduces the previous baseline exactly on all 28 gated series, so every delta is this PR’s own. The growth appears in every configuration that links the telomere library: release stripped file +1,728..+4,800 B and stripped .text +1,616..+4,672 B (wasi-threads largest); release-size stripped file +1,680..+13,520 B and stripped .text +1,600..+12,160 B, where release-size core-jit is the outlier — under the release-size profile’s optimisation settings the flattened handlers land differently in the one configuration that links both the interpreter and the JIT, while the same configuration grows least in the release profile (+2,064 B / +1,904 B); the per-configuration variation is the code-layout effect of the one library change, as in earlier re-baselines. The baseline configuration, which links no library code, is byte-identical in both profiles (4 of 28 gated series unchanged). Run-to-run spread was again 0 B for every gated series (14 profile/configuration rows x stripped file and stripped .text, n=3; the raw file and .text sizes were also identical across the three runs), so each threshold equals its observed baseline exactly (baseline + 0). Any further growth requires an intentional re-baseline; see docs/benchmarks/footprint.md, ‘Size regression gate (#164)’.
